title: v2.16 adds the ALBTargetControlConfig CRD and two pod webhooks for the ALB Target Optimizer agent — CRD and RBAC must be applied by hand

detection.reason: checked namespaces for the label elbv2.k8s.aws/alb-target-control-agent-injection=enabled — the webhooks' namespaceSelector (pods opt in with the label elbv2.k8s.aws/alb-target-control-agent-inject); labels, not annotations

quote: 🚨 🚨 🚨 For ALB Target Optimizer Users who want to use auto-injection for ALB target control agent: New CRD ALBTargetControlConfig has been added. Update your CRDs and RBAC. If you're upgrading the charts using helm upgrade, you need to update CRDs manually: `kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-load-balancer-controller/refs/heads/main/config/crd/bases/elbv2.k8s.aws_albtargetcontrolconfigs.yaml` also update rbac policy by applying the latest changes `kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-load-balancer-controller/refs/heads/main/config/rbac/role.yaml`
remediation: Only for ALB Target Optimizer users: apply config/crd/bases/elbv2.k8s.aws_albtargetcontrolconfigs.yaml and the latest config/rbac/role.yaml before enabling injection; everyone else is unaffected (the gate ALBTargetControlAgent is off by default).
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd albtargetcontrolconfigs.elbv2.k8s.aws -o name 2>/dev/null; kubectl get ns -l elbv2.k8s.aws/alb-target-control-agent-injection=enabled -o name; kubectl get pods -A -l elbv2.k8s.aws/alb-target-control-agent-inject=enabled -o name | head -20  # the CRD must exist wherever a namespace or pod carries the injection label
coversNotes: v2.16.0 (We're excited to announc): Introduced Target Optimizer for Application Load Balancers (
